headline: Bluefin: warm everywhere, no 64–68 break in the triangle
body:
Small-craft advisory for the outer waters holds until noon today, with 7–9 ft seas easing to 6–8 this afternoon out toward the Santa Rosa Flats and beyond; the channel itself is soft, 2–4 ft, and the triangle at midday reads 4.1 ft with light southerlies. Wednesday is the calmer day everywhere — channel 2–3 ft, the triangle near 3 ft, though a W breeze builds into the low teens by mid-afternoon.

Now the hard part: there's no 64–68 water anywhere on the chart. The triangle corners read 73.9 at the west corner, 73.7 at the east, and 71.7 at the south point down in the basin — warm through and through, the break slid off south and well past our numbers. Coolest water sampled is San Nicolas at 69.6, still above the band and not worth a 73 nm run for warm water. Neither day is a true bluefin day. If you go, take Wednesday's slick and grind the south point on the coolest edge — but temper the expectations.
